name: שבר מורכב – סכום שברים חלקי סכום שברים (באנגלית)

functions.name: igcd2
functions.body: if q=0 then abs(p) else igcd2(q,mod(p,q))

questiontext:
Express the following as a single fraction:

\(\displaystyle \frac{{{CT:0}}+{{CT:1}}}{{{CT:2}}+{{CT:3}}} =\) [[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]

Be sure to leave your answer as a single fraction in its simplest form.
generalfeedback:
Outline: Simplify the numerator and the denominator separately, each to a single fraction; then divide, by multiplying by the reciprocal, and cancel common factors.
Step 1 — The numerator
Both fractions are rewritten over the lowest common denominator of \({{CT:4}}\) and \({{CT:5}}\), which is \({{CT:6}}\):

\[ {{CT:0}}+{{CT:1}}=[[if test="{{CT:32}}"]]\frac{{{CT:7}}\cdot {{CT:8}}}{{{CT:4}}\cdot {{CT:8}}}[[else]]\frac{{{CT:7}}}{{{CT:4}}}[[/if]]+[[if test="{{CT:33}}"]]\frac{{{CT:9}}\cdot {{CT:10}}}{{{CT:5}}\cdot {{CT:10}}}[[else]]\frac{{{CT:9}}}{{{CT:5}}}[[/if]]=\frac{{{CT:11}}}{{{CT:6}}} \]

[[if test="{{CT:34}}"]]The numerator and the denominator have the common factor \(\gcd({{CT:11}},{{CT:6}})={{CT:12}}\), so we cancel it:

\[ \frac{{{CT:11}}}{{{CT:6}}}=\frac{{{CT:13}}}{{{CT:14}}} \]

[[else]]Here \(\gcd({{CT:11}},{{CT:6}})=1\), so nothing cancels.[[/if]]
Step 2 — The denominator
Both fractions are rewritten over the lowest common denominator of \({{CT:15}}\) and \({{CT:16}}\), which is \({{CT:17}}\):

\[ {{CT:2}}+{{CT:3}}=[[if test="{{CT:35}}"]]\frac{{{CT:18}}\cdot {{CT:19}}}{{{CT:15}}\cdot {{CT:19}}}[[else]]\frac{{{CT:18}}}{{{CT:15}}}[[/if]]+[[if test="{{CT:36}}"]]\frac{{{CT:20}}\cdot {{CT:21}}}{{{CT:16}}\cdot {{CT:21}}}[[else]]\frac{{{CT:20}}}{{{CT:16}}}[[/if]]=\frac{{{CT:22}}}{{{CT:17}}} \]

[[if test="{{CT:37}}"]]The numerator and the denominator have the common factor \(\gcd({{CT:22}},{{CT:17}})={{CT:23}}\), so we cancel it:

\[ \frac{{{CT:22}}}{{{CT:17}}}=\frac{{{CT:24}}}{{{CT:25}}} \]

[[else]]Here \(\gcd({{CT:22}},{{CT:17}})=1\), so nothing cancels.[[/if]]
Step 3 — Divide the two fractions
Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its reciprocal:

\[ \frac{{{CT:0}}+{{CT:1}}}{{{CT:2}}+{{CT:3}}}=\frac{{{CT:13}}}{{{CT:14}}}\div\frac{{{CT:24}}}{{{CT:25}}}=\frac{{{CT:13}}}{{{CT:14}}}\cdot\frac{{{CT:25}}}{{{CT:24}}}=\frac{{{CT:13}}\cdot {{CT:25}}}{{{CT:14}}\cdot {{CT:24}}}=\frac{{{CT:26}}}{{{CT:27}}} \]

[[if test="{{CT:38}}"]]Cancel the common factor \(\gcd({{CT:26}},{{CT:27}})={{CT:28}}\):

\[ \frac{{{CT:26}}}{{{CT:27}}}=\frac{{{CT:29}}\cdot {{CT:28}}}{{{CT:30}}\cdot {{CT:28}}}={{CT:31}} \]

[[else]]Here \(\gcd({{CT:26}},{{CT:27}})=1\), so the fraction is already in its simplest form.[[/if]] The answer, in its simplest form:

\[ \frac{{{CT:0}}+{{CT:1}}}{{{CT:2}}+{{CT:3}}}={{CT:31}} \]
